candidate.purpose: intervene on internal states of PyTorch models for interpretability, steering, robustness, model editing and causal-mechanism experiments

paper.title: pyvene: A Library for Understanding and Improving PyTorch Models via Interventions

observed_source_architecture: IntervenableModel wraps an existing PyTorch model and binds abstract RepresentationConfig locations to concrete module hooks.
Interventions are torch modules/functions and can be grouped into ordered serial/parallel intervention groups.
The core wrapper keeps per-intervention hook state, activation caches, hot activations, getter/setter call counters and intervention pointers.
IntervenableModelOutput separates original outputs, intervened outputs and collected activations.

The intervention catalog includes zeroing/subtraction-like controls, source swaps, rotated-space interventions, low-rank/trainable interventions, sigmoid masks, noise and autoencoder-latent interventions.
The package supports trainable interventions while freezing the wrapped model by default; intervention artifacts can be serialized separately from model weights.
Model-component dimensions and hook locations are mapped per supported architecture; the current head includes recent GQA head-dimension mapping fixes.

dependency_and_weight.assessment: Heavy for an F2 core causal-protocol dependency; acceptable only as an isolated experimental/model-analysis dependency if evidence later justifies it.

current_main_limitations_and_risks: Current F2-WP-507 explicitly does not observe hidden model state; pyvene does. Directly inserting pyvene into WP507 would cross the current scope boundary and could falsely equate model-internal perturbation with software-level GWT uptake.

Hook/component mappings are model-architecture specific. Recent 2026 GQA fixes show that dimension assumptions can be wrong for newer architectures, so exact target-model compatibility must be tested rather than assumed.
Upstream PR #110 for intervention scheduling across generated-token positions remains open. Dynamic generation-time intervention behavior must not be inferred from that unmerged PR.
Upstream PR #241 for nnsight/NDIF backend remains open. Remote/NDIF capability is not part of pinned main and is not an admitted F2 execution path.
The library carries a broad scientific Python/Transformers dependency surface that increases installation, versioning and reproducibility risk compared with a thin F2-native hook harness.
A changed model output after an internal intervention can reflect generic disruption, not the intended J-Space/GWT causal mechanism. Sham/random-location controls are mandatory.
pyvene state/caches/hooks are experimental runtime state only and must never become UnifiedDB or effect/completion authority.

why: WP507 is currently a deterministic message/workspace evidence contract, while pyvene is a model-internal intervention framework.
The strongest fit is later F2-WP-806 lesion/rescue and model-specific J-Space causal validation after an exact local model/J-Space ABI exists.

A thin F2-native experiment adapter can preserve F2 causal IDs and authority fences while borrowing pyvene-style intervention semantics; full library import should require measured benefit over that thinner adapter.
high_value_donor_mechanisms: explicit intervention vs control execution over the same base input
collect-original/intervened/activation outputs as separate experimental products
zero/swap/noise/mask interventions for lesion and rescue controls
serial/parallel multi-location interventions for mechanism specificity testing
trainable low-rank/rotated interventions as later research-only probes
serialized intervention configuration/artifact identity for reproducible experiments

target_workpackages.F2-WP-507: METHOD_DONOR_ONLY: strengthen matched intervention/control vocabulary; do not import hidden-state machinery into the current deterministic uptake contract.
target_workpackages.F2-WP-508: POTENTIAL_LATER_DONOR: pair workspace re-entry provenance with model-internal intervention receipts only if exact model call/J-Space identity is bound.
target_workpackages.F2-WP-806: STRONGEST_FIT: lesion/rescue harness for exact local model/J-Space experiments after model-specific runtime evidence exists.

f2_integration_assessment.authority_fence: pyvene experiment outputs are measurements/candidates only. They cannot mint world facts, GWT uptake truth, effect success, completion, canonical memory or whole-system acceptance.

counterhypotheses.statement: A thin F2-native forward-hook lesion harness provides all needed causal discriminators with much lower dependency and maintenance cost.
counterhypotheses.falsifier: On the exact target local model, pyvene materially improves intervention coverage, correctness or reproducibility over the thin harness while staying within acceptable latency/RAM/VRAM/dependency cost.

counterhypotheses.statement: Model-internal interventions are the wrong causal layer for proving F2 GWT uptake and will create misleading evidence.
counterhypotheses.falsifier: A pre-registered cross-layer experiment binds one exact F2 broadcast/J-Space control variable to one exact pyvene intervention and shows specific downstream changes with sham/random-location controls, while software-level uptake receipts remain independently satisfied.

counterhypotheses.statement: Exact approximately-0.8B target-model architecture is insufficiently supported or too brittle under pyvene hook mappings.
counterhypotheses.falsifier: Pinned target model passes deterministic collect/zero/swap/noise probes at declared components across repeated runs with exact activation-shape and output-digest receipts.

counterhypotheses.statement: Observed output changes are generic damage rather than mechanism-specific causal influence.
counterhypotheses.falsifier: Targeted intervention effect exceeds matched sham, random-layer, random-subspace and equal-norm noise controls and is reversible/rescuable at the pre-registered target.

next_discriminator.reason: No accepted F2 local-model/J-Space intervention ABI and no exact target-model runtime baseline are currently bound to this research object.
